The practice

A practice built around clarity under complexity.

I build web products and the systems underneath them, with a bias toward making complicated things legible — to the people who use them and the people who maintain them. Most of my work sits where interface design meets systems engineering: the seam where a good decision on one side quietly rescues the other.

The through-line across everything here is a belief that clarity is engineering work, not a coat of paint. A system that can be read is a system that can be operated, changed, and trusted. That principle shapes how I model data, name things, budget latency, and decide what an interface should refuse to show.

How I work

I prefer boring infrastructure and interesting product. I write migrations I can walk back. I treat performance as a design constraint decided early, not a metric patched late. And I try to leave every system a little more legible than I found it.

This site

This is where I think in public — case notes from real work, essays on the craft, and shorter field notes as they occur to me. It's built to be static, fast, and quiet, the same way I like the systems I work on.
